projects.title: NYS Extreme Heat Mapper and Heat Trends Explorer
projects.description: New York's Department of Environmental Conservation released two web tools, built with SUNY ESF and Davey Tree, that show neighborhood- and street-corridor-level temperatures for past and projected heat events and let users compare heat patterns across areas.
projects.why_interesting: Block-scale heat data for the whole state, with a technical advisory panel and added accessibility, is the kind of layer city planners can use directly for cooling-center and tree-planting decisions.

projects.title: Public School Match
projects.description: A free, independent tool that scores every NYC public school against one child's profile using public academic, demographic, admissions and commute data.
projects.why_interesting: Turns the scattered public school data into a single personalized ranking, outside any city-run portal.

projects.title: DeFlock open-source map of license plate reader cameras
projects.description: A New York Post story on Nassau County uses the crowdsourced DeFlock map to count more than 330 Flock Safety license plate readers on county roads, roughly one every 9.5 miles.
projects.why_interesting: A volunteer map of surveillance infrastructure is now feeding mainstream local reporting.

projects.title: BetaNYC open-source MCP connectors for city data
projects.description: BetaNYC published free connectors that let AI assistants query NYC Council legislation, city spending and contracts, 311 data, the City Record, the Charter and Administrative Code, and NYS Open Legislation.
projects.why_interesting: Puts a plain-language interface on the city's scattered civic datasets for non-coders.

projects.title: 2025 For Hire Vehicles and Green Taxi trip data
projects.description: The Taxi and Limousine Commission published the 2025 editions of its for-hire vehicle trip records (September 25) and green taxi trip records (September 28) on NYC Open Data.
projects.why_interesting: A full year of trip-level data after congestion pricing's first year, usable for pickup and traffic analysis.

projects.title: Paris metro and RER travel-time heatmap
projects.description: An interactive heatmap by Jules Grandin showing how long it takes to reach any point in the Paris region by metro and RER from a chosen station.
projects.why_interesting: A clean isochrone-style tool that makes transit access differences across the region visible at a glance.

projects.title: 15 minutes: the 15-minute city by walking speed
projects.description: Martin Bangratz's project shows how the reach of a 15-minute walk changes with walking speed and physical access.
projects.why_interesting: Challenges the one-size-fits-all assumption behind 15-minute-city metrics.

projects.title: Where Zurich rents run from 2,200 to 3,600 francs
projects.description: Tages-Anzeiger maps rents by Zurich neighborhood and shows the premium paid by people who move compared with long-term tenants.
projects.why_interesting: Separates the rent a neighborhood has from the rent a newcomer pays, a distinction most rent maps miss.

projects.title: How many times a week are Washington's streets swept?
projects.description: A chart of street-sweeping frequency across Washington, D.C. from the Cabinet of Infographic Curiosities.
projects.why_interesting: A small, concrete city-services dataset turned into a readable graphic; a template for other cities' sweeping schedules.

projects.title: Jurong Region Line construction graphic
projects.description: The Straits Times explains the engineering and terrain challenges of building Singapore's new Jurong Region Line.
projects.why_interesting: A good example of explaining a transit megaproject through its physical constraints.
